documentation.rationale: The identity and terms half is present: VIN decoded and matching, an all-fees-included price, and the dealer's quoted Carfax data. The maintenance half is absent: no receipts, no Carfax attached, no photos of at-risk areas. The listing also contradicts itself on accident history.

condition.rationale: Nothing mechanical is stated wrong, but nothing is proven. Photos show scuffed lower rear and front bumper areas (the front lower section possibly loose), a worn driver seat bolster and steering wheel, and an untidy interior. Two 2016 minor-damage events are disclosed without repair records.

price_value.rationale: At $14,520 the car sits about 9% below the low end of the $15,907–$19,565 fair value estimate and roughly 17% below its $17,441 mid. The discount is partly explained by the disclosed damage history, visible cosmetic wear and absent records, plus the cosmetic bumper work.

mission_fit.rationale: A 6-speed manual NC3 GT inside the $10,000-$19,000 ideal band, on a robust drivetrain with easy 6-24 month resale. It fits the enthusiast-bridge brief directly, provided a PPI clears it.

logistics.rationale: Maryland dealer, cross-country from Carmel. PPI access is not stated, though a mobile inspector is plausible. California out-of-state registration and smog add a step.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Top GT trim with a 6-speed manual, an apparent PRHT and a brown-leather interior are desirable NC3 traits. This is offset by scruffy cosmetics and a common black exterior.

evidence.mission_note: A 6-speed manual NC3 GT at $14,520 lands squarely in the enthusiast-bridge brief and budget band, with easy resale. Its fit depends on the damage history and condition checking out at a PPI.
evidence.rationale: The VIN decode confirms a 2014 MX-5 Grand Touring 2.0L, the photos show a manual shifter and an apparent PRHT, and the $14,520 price includes all dealer fees. The listing contradicts itself on accident history: the Autotrader summary reports none, while the dealer's own text cites two minor-damage events from 2016, and no repair records or Carfax are attached. The photos show cosmetic wear and damage, including lower rear bumper scuffing, a scraped and possibly loose front lower bumper section, a worn driver seat bolster and steering wheel, and an untidy interior. None of the five model-critical items has evidence: cooling system, OBD/readiness, PRHT function and dry floor, underbody, and drivetrain fluids. The price sits below the $15,907–$19,565 fair value range, which partly reflects these open questions. Single ownership and the clean title are dealer-quoted Carfax claims only.
evidence.next_action: Ask RockyCarZ for the full Carfax and written confirmation that an independent mobile PPI with a paint meter and underbody inspection can be done on the lot before any deposit.
